q: For the same billing cycle, does the firm's selected multiplier of 2.0 fall within the range SPP Doc. 204-A allows?
o: No, it goes over the ceiling of 1.8
SPP Doc. 204-A does not cap the multiplier for this method
No, it sits under the floor of 2.2
Yes, since 2.0 lies inside the permitted band of 1.5 to 2.5
n: Sec. 4.2 sets the multiplier range at 1.5 to 2.5; 2.0 falls squarely within that range and is therefore permissible. (Source: SPP Doc. 204-A, Sec. 4.2 / Formula section)
scenario: Under SPP Doc. 204-A, Sec. 4.2, a firm's Construction Supervision Group takes on fulltime supervision duties billed through the Multiple of Direct Personnel Expenses method. In a given billing period, the Architect logs 40 hours (AN) at ₱500 per hour, the Consultant logs 30 hours (CN) at ₱400 per hour, and the Technical Staff/Inspector logs 160 hours (TN) at ₱250 per hour. A multiplier (M) of 2.0 is applied by the office, and reimbursable expenses (R) for the period come to ₱15,000.

q: According to Sec. 5.1, which characterization fits the Construction Supervision Group (CSG)?
o: It always operates as a subsidiary firm of the Contractor
It functions as a government building-inspection office under the DPWH
It can be a qualified architectural firm, or a setup in which the Architect is merely one component
It must consist of a single, individually licensed architect working alone
n: Sec. 5.1 describes the CSG as one which may be a qualified architectural firm, or one of which the Architect is only part. (Source: SPP Doc. 204-A, Sec. 5.1)

q: Beyond holding the required degree, what else does Sec. 7.2 require of CSG Inspectors?
o: A separate PRC license issued specifically for building inspection
Substantial background in design and construction work, together with solid knowledge of building materials and construction detailing
Previous employment as a building official in a local government unit
Proficiency in at least one foreign language
n: Sec. 7.2 requires extensive experience in design and building construction, with strong knowledge of building materials and construction detailing. (Source: SPP Doc. 204-A, Sec. 7.2)

q: The specific tasks falling under each Sec. 2 scope-of-services item are spelled out in which document?
o: The Contractor's method statement
The Architect's Guidelines
The Owner's project manual
The IRR of the National Building Code
n: Sec. 2 closes by stating that the detailed tasks shall be as specified under the Architect's Guidelines. (Source: SPP Doc. 204-A, Sec. 2)

q: Applying the Direct Cost formula (AN + CN + TN) from SPP Doc. 204-A, how much is the Direct Cost for this billing period?
scenario: Under SPP Doc. 204-A, Sec. 4.2, a firm's Construction Supervision Group takes on fulltime supervision duties billed through the Multiple of Direct Personnel Expenses method. In a given billing period, the Architect logs 40 hours (AN) at ₱500 per hour, the Consultant logs 30 hours (CN) at ₱400 per hour, and the Technical Staff/Inspector logs 160 hours (TN) at ₱250 per hour. A multiplier (M) of 2.0 is applied by the office, and reimbursable expenses (R) for the period come to ₱15,000.

q: When an Owner has the Architect sit in on a project conference, inspect a candidate site, and discuss a possible investment, which SPP Doc. 204-A compensation method applies to that work?
o: Percentage of Project Construction Cost (Sec. 4.1)
Per Diem, Honorarium Plus Reimbursable Expenses (Sec. 4.5)
Multiple of Direct Personnel Expenses (Sec. 4.2)
Lump Sum or Fixed Fee (Sec. 4.4)
n: Sec. 4.5 covers exactly these activities — attending project-related meetings/conferences/trips (4.5.1), conducting ocular inspection of possible project sites (4.5.2), and conferring on prospective investments or ventures (4.5.3) — compensated on a per diem and honorarium basis plus out-of-pocket expenses. (Source: SPP Doc. 204-A, Sec. 4.5)

q: If a CSG's Service Contract/Agreement with the Owner involves it in reviewing, evaluating, and interpreting the Contract Documents during construction, does Sec. 6.2 still allow it to bear professional responsibility and civil liability notwithstanding Article 1723?
o: Yes, but liability attaches only when the CSG doubles as Architect-of-record
No, since only the Owner can ever answer for construction-phase disputes
No, Article 1723 blocks any liability for a CSG in every case
Yes — given this role, the Service Contract/Agreement may specifically provide for the CSG's professional responsibilities and civil liabilities
n: Sec. 6.2 states that a Service Contract/Agreement between the CSG and the Owner may stipulate certain professional responsibilities and civil liabilities of the CSG, particularly if the CSG is party to the review of the Contract Documents and their subsequent evaluation and interpretation during construction. (Source: SPP Doc. 204-A, Sec. 6.2)

q: Before full-time supervision groups became the norm, Sec. 1.3 says the Architect's construction-inspection assistant traditionally went by what title?
o: Project Coordinator
Clerk-of-Works
Site Superintendent
Resident Engineer
n: Sec. 1.3 recounts that when projects were still manageable in size, the Architect was assisted by a construction inspector traditionally called the Clerk-of-Works; as projects grew more complex, a full-time construction supervision group became necessary. (Source: SPP Doc. 204-A, Sec. 1.3)

q: Sec. 4.2 restricts the cost-based Multiple of Direct Personnel Expenses method to which category of work?
o: Purely creative architectural design work
Legal negotiation of contracts with the Contractor
Non-creative tasks like accounting, secretarial work, research, data gathering, and report writing
Structural engineering design work only
n: Sec. 4.2 limits this method to non-creative work (accounting, secretarial, research, data gathering, report preparation and the like), since the value of creative design cannot be measured by time spent. (Source: SPP Doc. 204-A, Sec. 4.2)

q: Per the definition of Reimbursable Expenses (R), printing costs for extra sets of drawings, reports, maps, and contract documents become billable to the Client only beyond how many submitted copies?
o: Printing is never a reimbursable cost
Ten (10) copies
Five (5) copies
Seven (7) copies
n: The formula section states that R includes the cost of printing extra sets of drawings, reports, maps, contract documents, etc., over the seven (7) copies submitted to the Client. (Source: SPP Doc. 204-A, Formula section (definition of R))

q: Sec. 5.2 forbids the CSG from deciding on matters that fall solely within whose responsibility?
o: The Architect-of-record (Aor)
The local government unit
The Contractor
The Owner's accountant
n: Sec. 5.2 states the CSG shall not make decisions on matters that are the sole responsibility of the Architect-of-record (Aor). (Source: SPP Doc. 204-A, Sec. 5.2)

q: SPP Document 204-A covers which service, and which prior issuance does it supersede?
o: Design-Build Services, a brand-new document with no earlier counterpart
Fulltime Supervision Services, superseding the 1979 UAP Doc. 204-A
Post-Construction Services, superseding the 1979 UAP Doc. 205
Predesign Services, superseding the 1979 UAP Doc. 201
n: SPP Document 204-A is captioned “Standard of Professional Practice on Fulltime Supervision Services” and is expressly noted as replacing the 1979 UAP Doc. 204-A. (Source: SPP Document 204-A, title block)

q: Under Sec. 3.2, what is the alternative (second) arrangement for delivering fulltime supervision services?
o: Serving as a subcontractor hired directly by the Contractor
Serving exclusively under a design-build setup
Serving purely as an unpaid volunteer inspector for the Owner
Serving strictly as Consulting Architect for fulltime supervision, or as the CSG, apart from also being Aor
n: Sec. 3.2 provides the second manner: working as Consulting Architect for fulltime supervision services only, or as the CSG, distinct from the dual-capacity arrangement under Sec. 3.1. (Source: SPP Doc. 204-A, Sec. 3.2)

q: For the same billing period, what Total Cost of Service is billed to the Client?
n: Total Cost of Service = Fee + R = ₱144,000 + ₱15,000 (reimbursable expenses) = ₱159,000. (Source: SPP Doc. 204-A, Formula section (Total Cost of Service = Fee + R))
scenario: Under SPP Doc. 204-A, Sec. 4.2, a firm's Construction Supervision Group takes on fulltime supervision duties billed through the Multiple of Direct Personnel Expenses method. In a given billing period, the Architect logs 40 hours (AN) at ₱500 per hour, the Consultant logs 30 hours (CN) at ₱400 per hour, and the Technical Staff/Inspector logs 160 hours (TN) at ₱250 per hour. A multiplier (M) of 2.0 is applied by the office, and reimbursable expenses (R) for the period come to ₱15,000.

q: What stance does Sec. 4.6 (Mixed Methods of Compensation) take on selecting a compensation method for a project?
o: It restricts mixing of methods to government-funded projects only
It flatly bans combining compensation methods
It allows only one fixed method per project without exception
It recognizes more than one compensation method and calls for each project to be assessed to find the most fitting one
n: Sec. 4.6 states the SPP provides for more than one method of compensation on a project, and each project should be examined to determine the most appropriate method. (Source: SPP Doc. 204-A, Sec. 4.6)

q: Sec. 7.1 sets what minimum academic credential for CSG Inspectors?
o: A Bachelor of Science in Civil Engineering
A Bachelor of Science in Architecture (B.S. Arch.)
A Master's degree in Architecture
Any bachelor's degree paired with on-the-job training
n: Sec. 7.1 requires CSG Inspectors to hold a Bachelor of Science in Architecture (B.S. Arch.) degree. (Source: SPP Doc. 204-A, Sec. 7.1)

q: Which item below falls outside the CSG's Scope of Services as listed in Sec. 2?
o: Evaluation of construction work
Design development of the architectural plans
Quality control
Preparation of daily inspection reports and filing of documents
n: Sec. 2 lists four scope items: Quality Control, Evaluation of Construction Work, Preparation of Daily Inspection Reports, and Filing of Documents. Design development is a design-phase service, not part of fulltime supervision's scope. (Source: SPP Doc. 204-A, Sec. 2)

q: Before settling on the Multiple of Direct Personnel Expenses method, Sec. 4.2 requires the Architect to reveal what to the Client at the outset?
o: Only a final lump-sum figure, with no itemized breakdown
The Architect's tax identification number
The rates of the professionals/personnel to be assigned and the multiplier that will apply
The home addresses of all staff assigned to the project
n: Sec. 4.2 requires the Architect to make known to the Client, at the start of the commission, the rate of professionals/personnel assigned and the multiplier to be applied before agreeing on this method. (Source: SPP Doc. 204-A, Sec. 4.2)

q: Sec. 4.4 notes the Lump Sum or Fixed Fee method suits which type of project in particular?
o: Government projects, given the heavier paperwork and time demands involved
Small-scale residential renovation work
International projects staffed with foreign consultants
Emergency disaster-response projects
n: Sec. 4.4 states this method may be applied to government projects since they entail more paper work and time-consuming efforts. (Source: SPP Doc. 204-A, Sec. 4.4)

q: Sec. 6.2 explains that, under Civil Code Article 1723, the CSG can seem to carry no legal responsibility for what reason?
o: Article 1723 applies exclusively to government-funded work
Design accountability rests with the Aor and Eors, while construction accountability rests with the Contractor
CSGs are, under the law, never subject to a written service contract
Article 1723 confers total immunity from suit on every CSG
n: Sec. 6.2 explains that under Article 1723 of the Civil Code, the CSG may appear to have no legal responsibility since the Aor and Eors are responsible for the design and the Contractor for the construction. (Source: SPP Doc. 204-A, Sec. 6.2)

q: According to Sec. 1.2, who bears direct professional responsibility and liability for supervising construction of the project?
o: The Contractor's project superintendent
The city or municipal building official
The Architect-in-charge of construction (Aicc)
The Engineer-of-record (Eor), acting alone
n: Sec. 1.2 states that the Architect-in-charge of construction (Aicc) is directly and professionally responsible and liable for the construction supervision of the project. (Source: SPP Doc. 204-A, Sec. 1.2)

q: The Architect's Fee for Fulltime Supervision computed as a Percentage of PCC is spelled out in what document per Sec. 4.1?
o: The Owner's procurement manual
Article 1723 of the Civil Code
The Architect's Guidelines
The Uniform Code of Ethics
n: Sec. 4.1 states that the Architect's Fee for Fulltime Supervision based on the PCC shall be detailed in the Architect's Guidelines. (Source: SPP Doc. 204-A, Sec. 4.1)

q: When a CSG technical staff member posted 150 km from the Architect's area of operation runs up per diem and lodging costs, can these be billed to the Client as reimbursable expenses (R)?
o: No, since only foreign consultants' housing and living allowances ever qualify
Yes, because the formula in Sec. 4 treats costs as reimbursable once the assignment exceeds 100 km from the Architect's area of operation
Only when the project Owner is a government agency
No, such costs are already folded entirely into the Fee
n: The formula section defines R to include transportation, per diem, housing and living allowance of local consultants and technical staff assigned to places over 100 km from the Architect's area of operation. (Source: SPP Doc. 204-A, Formula section (definition of R))

q: Which role does Sec. 5.1 specifically bar the CSG from taking on?
o: The Owner's authorized representative for permit matters
Local building official
The Contractor's project superintendent
Architect-of-record (Aor)
n: Sec. 5.1 provides that the CSG shall not assume the responsibility of the Contractor's project superintendent. (Source: SPP Doc. 204-A, Sec. 5.1)

q: As with the rest of the 2010 SPP series, SPP Doc. 204-A implements the IRR of which statute, and on what date did it take effect?
o: An internal UAP guideline with no basis in any statute
R.A. No. 9266, published and made effective in 2004, the year it was enacted
R.A. No. 545, effective immediately upon its 1950 signing
R.A. No. 9266 (The Architecture Act of 2004), published 21 February 2011 and effective 09 March 2011
n: The SPP series states it is Part of the IRR of R.A. No. 9266 (The Architecture Act of 2004) and was published 21 February 2011 in the Official Gazette, taking effect 09 March 2011. (Source: SPP Doc. 204-A / SPP series, footer notice)

q: When the Architect doubles as both Aor and the Consulting Architect for fulltime supervision (or the CSG), Sec. 3.1 says this dual role is advantageous for what reason?
o: The Aor legally owns the construction site for the project's duration
The Aor is the only party authorized to fix the Contractor's price
The Aor becomes, by default, an employee of the Owner under labor law
The Aor can better interpret his own drawings and documents and ensure the Contractor follows them
n: Sec. 3.1 explains that as Architect-of-record, the Aor is in a better position to interpret his own drawings and documents and to assure conformity by the Contractor, and may assign staff to perform the fulltime supervisory work per the Architect's Guidelines. (Source: SPP Doc. 204-A, Sec. 3.1)

q: Using Fee = Direct Cost × M for the same billing period, what does the Fee amount to?
n: Fee = Direct Cost (₱72,000) × M (2.0) = ₱144,000. (Source: SPP Doc. 204-A, Formula section (Fee = Direct Cost x M))
scenario: Under SPP Doc. 204-A, Sec. 4.2, a firm's Construction Supervision Group takes on fulltime supervision duties billed through the Multiple of Direct Personnel Expenses method. In a given billing period, the Architect logs 40 hours (AN) at ₱500 per hour, the Consultant logs 30 hours (CN) at ₱400 per hour, and the Technical Staff/Inspector logs 160 hours (TN) at ₱250 per hour. A multiplier (M) of 2.0 is applied by the office, and reimbursable expenses (R) for the period come to ₱15,000.

q: Which activity below is absent from Sec. 4.5's list of tasks paid on a per diem/honorarium basis?
o: Attending project-related meetings, conferences, or trips
On-site supervision of structural concrete pouring
Discussing prospective investments or ventures with others
Conducting ocular inspection of possible project sites
n: Sec. 4.5.1–4.5.3 list only attending meetings/conferences/trips, ocular inspection of possible sites, and conferring on prospective investments/ventures. On-site concrete-pouring supervision is a fulltime-supervision scope task, not a Sec. 4.5 activity. (Source: SPP Doc. 204-A, Sec. 4.5.1–4.5.3)

q: If an Owner sues the Aor (and Eors) and the Contractor over civil liability traceable to the CSG's acts, what remedy does Sec. 6.3 give the Aor and Eors?
o: Terminating the CSG's service contract as their sole option
Filing cross claims against the CSG
Reporting the CSG to the PRC Board, with no further remedy
Absorbing the liability, since no legal recourse exists
n: Sec. 6.3 provides that if the Aor (and Eors) and the Contractor are sued by an Owner for civil liabilities due to acts traceable to the CSG, the Aor and Eors may file cross claims against the CSG. (Source: SPP Doc. 204-A, Sec. 6.3)

q: How does Sec. 1.4 describe the engagement of the CSG, and to whom must it answer?
o: Chosen by the Owner alone, with no role for the Architect
Put in place by the local building official, answerable to government alone
Recommended by the Architect and hired by the Owner, answerable to both
Hired straight by the Contractor, answerable only to the Contractor
n: Sec. 1.4 provides that the CSG is normally recommended by the Architect (based on performance) and hired by the Owner, and is answerable to both the Owner and the Architect. (Source: SPP Doc. 204-A, Sec. 1.4)

q: What band does Sec. 4.2 set for the multiplier (M) that covers overhead and profit?
n: Sec. 4.2 (and the formula section) states the multiplier ranges from 1.5 to 2.5, depending on office set-up, overhead, experience, and project complexity. (Source: SPP Doc. 204-A, Sec. 4.2)

q: Sec. 4.3 says the Professional Fee Plus Expenses method is commonly used under what circumstance?
o: For emergency, post-disaster repair work only
Where an ongoing relationship covers a series of projects
Exclusively on government infrastructure projects
For a single, one-off small residential renovation
n: Sec. 4.3 states this method is frequently used where there is a continuing relationship involving a series of projects, establishing a fixed sum over and above reimbursement for the Architect's technical time and overhead. (Source: SPP Doc. 204-A, Sec. 4.3)

q: Sec. 6.1 splits the CSG's legal responsibility between the Owner and the Aor in what way?
o: The CSG answers to the Contractor for both administrative and technical matters
The CSG answers to the Owner for administrative matters only, and to the Aor for technical matters
The CSG answers to the Owner for both administrative and technical matters
The CSG answers to the Aor for administrative matters and to the Owner for technical matters
n: Sec. 6.1 states the CSG is responsible to the Owner only for administrative matters; for technical matters, the CSG is responsible to the Aor. (Source: SPP Doc. 204-A, Sec. 6.1)

q: Sec. 1.1 names four principal parties in the design-and-construction process. Which one below is not among them?
o: The Owner, who commissions the project
The Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH)
The Architect together with his Specialist Consultants (SCs)
The Contractor, who carries out the construction
n: Sec. 1.1 lists only four members: the Owner; the Architect and his SCs; the Contractor; and the individual or group who assist in the supervision and delivery of the work. DPWH is not among them. (Source: SPP Doc. 204-A, Sec. 1.1)

q: Sec. 4 grounds the Architect's compensation for Fulltime Supervision Services on what general basis?
o: A single government-set rate uniform for all architects
The Architect's/firm's talent, skill, and experience, together with the type and level of services rendered
Purely the number of years the Architect has held a license
Purely the project's floor area in square meters
n: Sec. 4 states compensation is based on the Architect's/architectural firm's talents, skill, experience, and on the type and level of professional services provided. (Source: SPP Doc. 204-A, Sec. 4)
